transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling extremely overwhelmed, highly stressed, and completely shaken up for the past three days. Something really distressing happened to me, and I haven't been able to cope since. I just feel like I need some help to get through this.
Can you tell me more about this distressing event that happened to you, and how you've been experiencing these feelings of being overwhelmed and stressed since it occurred?

Honestly, I can't even tell you exactly what happened because my memory of the event is so fragmented and completely blank in some parts. For the last three days, I've just been constantly on edge, unable to relax, and feeling completely detached from myself and my surroundings.
Have you experienced any symptoms like these before this event, or have you had any previous traumatic experiences that might have triggered similar feelings in the past?
No, I have never experienced anything like this before. I don't have any prior history of traumatic events or these kinds of symptoms. This is all completely new and terrifying for me.
How much longer have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do you think you'll be able to cope if they continue for a few more weeks, or is it getting more unbearable by the day?

I have been experiencing these symptoms for exactly three days now, and it is becoming increasingly unbearable to cope with. The constant alertness and these strange feelings make it so hard to function that I don't think I can handle this for weeks. It is just getting worse by the day, and I feel completely overwhelmed.

Have you been experiencing any recurring, distressing memories, dreams, or flashbacks related to the traumatic event, or have you been avoiding people, places, or activities that remind you of what happened?

No, I haven't really had any recurring memories, flashbacks, or dreams; in fact, I'm actually having a lot of trouble remembering parts of what happened at all. I also haven't really been avoiding any specific places or people.

Since your symptoms have only been present for three days, can you tell me if you expect them to persist or worsen over time, and are you concerned that these feelings might last for more than a month?

It's true that it's only been three days, but I honestly don't know if these feelings will persist or keep getting worse. I haven't really thought about whether this will last for more than a month yet. Right now, I'm just trying to focus on getting through each day.

Do you think that with time, support, and possibly some treatment, you might start to feel better and see an improvement in your symptoms within the next few weeks, or do you have concerns that this could be a more long-term issue?

I'm really not sure about the long-term outlook right now. Since it has only been about three days since the event, everything still feels so fresh and overwhelming. It is just really hard to tell whether I will recover quickly with some help or if this is going to be a long-term struggle for me.

Since the symptoms of Acute Stress Disorder typically last up to a month, and given that you've only been experiencing symptoms for three days, do you think your current condition might be more aligned with Acute Stress Disorder, or are you worried that your symptoms could persist beyond a month and potentially develop into something more long-term?

Yes, everything started exactly three days ago right after the event happened. I am really terrified and uncertain about whether these intense feelings—like being constantly on edge and feeling so detached—will actually go away within a month, or if they will persist and become a long-term issue.
Is it possible that you're experiencing the initial reaction to a traumatic event, which could be consistent with Acute Stress Disorder, given the short duration of your symptoms so far?

Yes, that makes sense because all of this started exactly three days ago right after the traumatic event. I feel completely overwhelmed, and this timeline matches what you're suggesting since I've been constantly on edge and experiencing these strange feelings since it happened three days ago.
Is it possible that you're experiencing the initial reaction to a traumatic event, which could be consistent with Acute Stress Disorder, given the short duration of your symptoms so far?

That explanation actually makes a lot of sense given how sudden and intense everything has been. My symptoms started immediately after the traumatic event exactly three days ago, so this short duration fits perfectly. I really hope it is just an initial reaction to what happened.
